benchmark:
Dev machine (AMD Ryzen 5 7530U, Linux 7.0, Node 24.13.1, V8 13.6), medians of 15 runs at load average 4 to 6. These numbers must be re-run on the lab machine. Values are ns per operation, measured in batches of 1,000.
- push+shift (half full), mean / p50 / p95: n=10^3 (capacity 1,024): 5.06 / 4.66 / 8.67; n=10^4 (16,384): 5.85 / 5.42 / 9.59; n=10^5 (131,072): 6.08 / 5.36 / 10.42. The ratio t(10^5)/t(10^3) has a median of 1.12 and a worst of 1.61 against the 2.0 limit.
- push when full (overwrite), mean: 4.97, 5.13 and 4.58 at 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5. Ratio median 0.94, worst 1.36.
- The curve is flat, as expected for O(1): about 5 ns from 10^3 to 10^5.
- Budgets: 6 ns per push/shift pair against ≤ 50 ns (pass). ByteRing with 4 KiB chunks has a median of 15,343 MB/s (range 1,867 to 22,492; final run 2,549) against ≥ 500 MB/s (pass).
- Bytes per entry (allocated / used from stats(), measured with --expose-gc): 10^3: 8.19 / 8.00, measured 8.78; 10^4: 13.11 / 8.00, measured 13.31; 10^5: 10.49 / 8.00, measured 10.54. Used is exactly 8 B/entry. The extra allocated space comes only from rounding the capacity up to a power of two.
- Float64Ring percentile(0.95) over 1,024 values takes about 27 µs.
The full table, proofs and the filled DSA.md entry are in dsa/src/ringbuffer/README.md.
test_changes:
No existing assertion was changed or removed.
(1) dsa/bench/ringbuffer.bench.ts: the two timed loops now read BATCH from a local constant set outside the timed closure. Under Vitest's module runner every read of an imported binding is a getter call. Vitest warned "accessed module export getters too many times", and that getter cost about 25 ns per iteration against a real ring cost of 5 to 7 ns (30 ns reported vs about 5 ns in plain Node), which also flattened the curve. The shape limits (≤ 2) and budgets are unchanged.
(2) dsa/tests/ringbuffer.prop.test.ts: both properties get an explicit timeout, PROP_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s + 30 ms × PROP.numRuns. The spec's nightly PLT_PROP_RUNS=10000 takes about 25 s and always failed Vitest's 5 s default, and 1,000 runs under coverage took 4.6 s. The ring accounts for only about 24 ms of each 1,000 runs; the rest is fast-check and deep toEqual. I also added the property "DSA-RING-01 Float64Ring matches RingBuffer<number> on random push, tryPush, shift, at and clear in both modes", a differential test with arbitrary doubles including -0, NaN and ±∞.
(3) dsa/tests/ringbuffer.test.ts: 2 tests added. "DSA-RING-01 Float64Ring supports the whole Ring API in reject mode, iteration follows toArray after a wrap, and stats() is exact" also checks that an unknown mode throws INVALID. "DSA-RING-01 Float64Ring nearest-rank percentile is exact where q·n rounds past an integer": 0.3·10 = 3.0000000000000004, so a plain ceil would pick the wrong rank.
(4) All 4 files were formatted with the repo's Prettier config.
